questions.stem: News of the discovery set off a media (   ) that lasted for almost a fortnight. News outlets sent reporters to the site from across the country.

questions.stem: A: Have residents accepted the company's public apology? B: No; it did little to (   ) their anger after weeks of complaints.

questions.stem: The study examined whether (   ) messages in television advertising really affect what ordinary shoppers buy. The images were designed to influence viewers without their awareness.
questions.translation: その研究は、テレビ広告の中の潜在意識に働きかけるメッセージが一般の買い物客の購買に本当に影響するかどうかを調べた。 その映像は、視聴者が気づかないうちに影響を与えるよう作られていた。

questions.stem: His reply was so (   ) that the visitor assumed she had offended him somehow. The visitor left quickly after hearing the answer.
questions.translation: 彼の返事があまりにぶっきらぼうだったので、訪問者は自分が何か彼の気分を害したのだと思った。 訪問者はその返事を聞くとすぐに立ち去った。

questions.stem: The soup was barely (   ), but the climbers were far too hungry to complain. The climbers ate it because no other meal was available.
questions.translation: そのスープはかろうじて口にできる程度だったが、登山者たちは空腹すぎて文句を言わなかった。 他に食事がなかったので、登山者たちはそれを食べた。

questions.stem: A (   ) glance at the accounts was enough to show that something was wrong. A closer audit was scheduled for the following morning.
questions.translation: 帳簿をざっと一瞥しただけで、何かがおかしいと分かった。 翌朝、より詳しい監査が予定された。

questions.stem: The new coating makes the fabric (   ) to water without trapping any heat inside the jacket. Water ran off the surface without entering the material.

questions.stem: For weeks, older colleagues (   ) the young apprentice until he finally agreed to enter the national competition. The apprentice finally agreed to enter the national competition.

questions.stem: The campaign gradually (   ) after its two main organizers moved to other cities for work. Without its organizers, the campaign lost momentum and ended quietly.
